name: Alcimus
charge: Slandering Judas to the king; slaying sixty Asideans under a sworn peace; pulling down the wall of the inner court
summary: When Demetrius was set on the throne, all the wicked and ungodly men of Israel came to him, having Alcimus, who desired to be high priest, for their captain, and they accused the people, saying that Judas and his brethren had slain the king’s friends and driven them out of their own land (1 Maccabees 7:5-7). The king sent Bacchides with Alcimus, whom he made high priest, commanding him to take vengeance on the children of Israel (1 Maccabees 7:8-9). Under a sworn peace Alcimus took sixty of the Assideans and slew them in one day, and afterward, when he commanded the wall of the inner court of the sanctuary to be pulled down, he was struck with a palsy and died in great torment (1 Maccabees 7:12-18; 1 Maccabees 9:54-56).
offenseFull: The teaching keeps a list running through this period and puts him at the end of it: Simon of the tribe of Benjamin, Jason, Menelaus, Rhodocus, and now Alcimus. The wicked among our own always seek position. The men who came with him to Demetrius had been driven out of the land, because they were of no use to their own people and of no use to the king they sold them to; their complaint was that Judas had slain the king’s friends (1 Maccabees 7:5-7). The king made him high priest and sent Bacchides with him and a great power into the land of Judea, with a commandment to take vengeance on the children of Israel (1 Maccabees 7:8-9). They sent to Judas and his brethren with peaceable words deceitfully, but he gave no heed, seeing that they had come with a great power (1 Maccabees 7:10-11).

The Assideans were the first among the children of Israel to seek peace of them, saying that one that is a priest of the seed of Aaron had come with the army and would do them no wrong (1 Maccabees 7:12-14). The teaching stops on that reasoning, because it is the mistake: he was in the line, but he had defiled himself willingly in the times of their mingling with the Gentiles, and a man in the line who has done that is not what the line says he is. He spoke to them peaceably and swore that he would not seek harm to them or to their friends, and they believed him, and he took sixty of them and slew them in one day (1 Maccabees 7:15-16). The writer reaches for the psalm to say what it looked like, that the flesh of the saints was cast out and their blood shed round about Jerusalem with none to bury them (1 Maccabees 7:17; Psalms 79:2-3). Then the fear and dread of them fell on all the people, who said that there was neither truth nor righteousness in them, for they had broken the covenant and the oath they had made (1 Maccabees 7:18). Bacchides slew many and cast them into the great pit, committed the country to Alcimus, and left him a power to aid him (1 Maccabees 7:19-20).

Alcimus contended for the high priesthood, and all such as troubled the people resorted to him, and when they had gotten the land of Juda into their power they did much hurt in Israel, so that Judas saw that Alcimus and his company had done among the Israelites even above the heathen (1 Maccabees 7:21-23). The teaching does not flinch from that verse: a man of the nation can do us worse than the nations. When Judas took vengeance on the men who had revolted, and Alcimus saw that he had the upper hand and could not abide his force, he went again to the king and said all the worst of them that he could (1 Maccabees 7:24-25). The second book shows the same speech. He came to Demetrius with a crown of gold and a palm and boughs used solemnly in the temple, and in council he said that those called Assideans, whose captain is Judas Maccabeus, nourish war and will not let the realm be in peace, that he himself had been deprived of his ancestors’ honour, meaning the high priesthood, and that as long as Judas lives it is not possible that the state should be quiet (2 Maccabees 14:3-10; 2 Maccabees 14:26-27).
judgmentFull: In the hundred fifty and third year, in the second month, Alcimus commanded that the wall of the inner court of the sanctuary should be pulled down, and he pulled down also the works of the prophets (1 Maccabees 9:54). That is where it ended. As he began to pull down, at that very time he was plagued and his enterprises hindered, for his mouth was stopped and he was taken with a palsy, so that he could no more speak nor give order concerning his house (1 Maccabees 9:55). So Alcimus died at that time with great torment (1 Maccabees 9:56).

The mouth that had slandered his own nation to two kings was stopped first, and the man who had sworn a peace and killed sixty men under it was left unable to give an order about his own house. When Bacchides saw that Alcimus was dead he returned to the king, and the land of Juda was in rest two years (1 Maccabees 9:57). The teaching reads the case as a warning to men who want the office more than the work: he had the pedigree, took the title from a foreign king, held the country with a foreign garrison, and the record of it is four verses about how he died.

taught.title: Psalm 79: The Heathen Have Defiled Thy Inheritance

lawsResolved.text: You shall make no false or deceitful oath or covenant.
God will judge and punish false swearers.
If a man acts with premeditation against his neighbor, to kill him with guile, he shall die.
You shall not go about speaking slander or spreading false reports about others.
Priests are to keep the charge of the sanctuary and tabernacle of the congregation and keep it supplied and in proper order.
Priests are not to defile or profane themselves.
You shall not bear false witness against another nor raise a false report.

text.text: There came unto him all the wicked and ungodly men of Israel, having Alcimus, who was desirous to be high priest, for their captain:
And they accused the people to the king, saying, Judas and his brethren have slain all thy friends, and driven us out of our own land.
Now therefore send some man whom thou trustest, and let him go and see what havock he hath made among us, and in the king’s land, and let him punish them with all them that aid them.
Then the king chose Bacchides, a friend of the king, who ruled beyond the flood, and was a great man in the kingdom, and faithful to the king,
And him he sent with that wicked Alcimus, whom he made high priest, and commanded that he should take vengeance of the children of Israel.
So they departed, and came with a great power into the land of Judea, where they sent messengers to Judas and his brethren with peaceable words deceitfully.
But they gave no heed to their words; for they saw that they were come with a great power.
Then did there assemble unto Alcimus and Bacchides a company of scribes, to require justice.
Now the Assideans were the first among the children of Israel that sought peace of them:
For said they, One that is a priest of the seed of Aaron is come with this army, and he will do us no wrong.
So he spake unto them, peaceably, and sware unto them, saying, we will procure the harm neither of you nor your friends.
Whereupon they believed him: howbeit he took of them threescore men, and slew them in one day, according to the words which he wrote,
The flesh of thy saints have they cast out, and their blood have they shed round about Jerusalem, and there was none to bury them.
Wherefore the fear and dread of them fell upon all the people, who said, There is neither truth nor righteousness in them; for they have broken the covenant and oath that they made.
The dead bodies of thy servants have they given to be meat unto the fowls of the heaven, the flesh of thy saints unto the beasts of the earth.
Their blood have they shed like water round about Jerusalem; and there was none to bury them.

After this, removed Bacchides from Jerusalem, and pitched his tents in Bezeth, where he sent and took many of the men that had forsaken him, and certain of the people also, and when he had slain them, he cast them into the great pit.
Then committed he the country to Alcimus, and left with him a power to aid him: so Bacchides went to the king.
But Alcimus contended for the high priesthood.
And unto him resorted all such as troubled the people, who, after they had gotten the land of Juda into their power, did much hurt in Israel.
Now when Judas saw all the mischief that Alcimus and his company had done among the Israelites, even above the heathen,
He went out into all the coasts of Judea round about, and took vengeance of them that had revolted from him, so that they durst no more go forth into the country.

On the other side, when Alcimus saw that Judas and his company had gotten the upper hand, and knew that he was not able to abide their force, he went again to the king, and said all the worst of them that he could.

Now one Alcimus, who had been high priest, and had defiled himself wilfully in the times of their mingling with the Gentiles, seeing that by no means he could save himself, nor have any more access to the holy altar,

Came to king Demetrius in the hundred and one and fiftieth year, presenting unto him a crown of gold, and a palm, and also of the boughs which were used solemnly in the temple: and so that day he held his peace.
Howbeit having gotten opportunity to further his foolish enterprize, and being called into counsel by Demetrius, and asked how the Jews stood affected, and what they intended, he answered thereunto:
Those of the Jews that he called Assideans, whose captain is Judas Maccabeus, nourish war and are seditious, and will not let the rest be in peace.
Therefore I, being deprived of mine ancestors’ honour, I mean the high priesthood, am now come hither:

First, verily for the unfeigned care I have of things pertaining to the king; and secondly, even for that I intend the good of mine own countrymen: for all our nation is in no small misery through the unadvised dealing of them aforesaid.
Wherefore, O king, seeing knowest all these things, be careful for the country, and our nation, which is pressed on every side, according to the clemency that thou readily shewest unto all.
For as long as Judas liveth, it is not possible that the state should be quiet.

But Alcimus, perceiving the love that was betwixt them, and considering the covenants that were made, came to Demetrius, and told him that Nicanor was not well affected toward the state; for that he had ordained Judas, a traitor to his realm, to be the king’s successor.

Then the king being in a rage, and provoked with the accusations of the most wicked man, wrote to Nicanor, signifying that he was much displeased with the covenants, and commanding him that he should send Maccabeus prisoner in all haste unto Antioch.

Moreover in the hundred fifty and third year, in the second month, Alcimus commanded that the wall of the inner court of the sanctuary should be pulled down; he pulled down also the works of the prophets

And as he began to pull down, even at that time was Alcimus plagued, and his enterprizes hindered: for his mouth was stopped, and he was taken with a palsy, so that he could no more speak any thing, nor give order concerning his house.
So Alcimus died at that time with great torment.
Now when Bacchides saw that Alcimus was dead, he returned to the king: whereupon the land of Judea was in rest two years.
